extract:
Fito y Fitipaldis is the band led by Adolfo "Fito" Cabrales, a singer, guitarist and songwriter from Bilbao in the Basque Country. Cabrales was already well known as the frontman of Platero y Tú, one of the defining groups of the hard-edged Basque and Spanish rock scene of the 1990s. He launched Fito y Fitipaldis in 1998 as a side outlet for songs that did not fit Platero's electric, riff-driven style. Over the following years the project became his main vehicle, and it has remained active from the late 1990s into the 2020s.

The project grew from Cabrales's affection for roots rock, soul and blues, the strain of music running from the Rolling Stones to Spanish street-rock figures such as Rosendo. Within the Basque scene he also had close ties to Robe Iniesta of Extremoduro, with whom he formed the one-off project Extrechinato y Tú. The debut, A Puerta Cerrada (1998), introduced a looser, warmer sound built on piano, saxophone and slide guitar. Saxophonist Javier Alzola became a signature voice of the band, and guitarist and producer Carlos Raya became Cabrales's key creative partner.

Los Sueños Locos (2001) arrived around the time Platero y Tú wound down, and songs like "La casa por el tejado" signalled that the band was ready to stand on its own. The commercial breakthrough came with Lo más lejos a tu lado, home to "Soldadito marinero," which became one of the most widely sung Spanish rock songs of the decade. The live album Vivo... para contarlo captured the band's growing stadium-level following. Por la boca vive el pez (2006) followed, and its title track, along with "Me equivocaría otra vez," cemented Cabrales as a major figure in mainstream Spanish rock. The band's catalogue appeared on DRO, part of the Warner group.

Collaboration has been a recurring thread. In 2008 Cabrales joined Argentine songwriter Andrés Calamaro on "Whisky barato" for the duets record 2 son multitud. Antes de que cuente diez (2009) kept the Raya-produced blend of rock, rhythm and blues and ballads. Its era also produced singles such as "Los huesos de los besos" and "Me acordé de ti." Huyendo conmigo de mí (2014) was led by "Entre la espada y la pared" and showed a more reflective, mature songwriter. That same year the band released a live recording from Bilbao's Teatro Arriaga, which included the song "Cerca de las vías." In 2015 came a special edition recorded at Madrid's Las Ventas bullring.

Critics and audiences have generally credited Fito y Fitipaldis with bringing an earthy, classic rock and roll sensibility to the top of the Spanish charts. Cabrales's plain-spoken lyrics, full of street imagery, everyday love and self-deprecation, connect the rock urbano tradition with a broad pop audience. His records have regularly topped Spanish sales charts, and his tours fill arenas and bullrings across Spain.

The band returned with Cada vez cadáver in 2021 and continues to tour. Its legacy rests on proving that a veteran of the Basque rock underground could reinvent himself without abandoning his roots. Along the way Cabrales built a catalogue of songs that have become standards for a generation of Spanish rock listeners.
title: Fito y Fitipaldis
